messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT HIGH - streaming.p99 spike detected in us-west-2. SLO breach (p99 > 2.5s) for model 'redwood-base-v2' on host gpu-node-32. Paging on-call: @sarah (oncall). Incident page: https://incidents.redwood.example/INC-20260315-42 :rotating_light:

sarah (oncall): acked. jumping in. can someone grab quick impact numbers?

mike-sre: seeing p95 ~600ms, p99 ~3.4s over last 5m, error rate up 0.4%. Streaming stalls: TCP streams with stalled kernel writes on gpu-node-32 queue.

alice-eng: good catch. any recent deploys? deploy-bot: deploy 2026-03-15T08:42 UTC to canary of routing service.

sarah (oncall): rolling back canary?

mike-sre: traffic pattern looks same across other nodes, but only gpu-node-32 shows huge tail. suspect hardware throttle/ECC. fetching node telemetry.

mike-sre: `ssh accel@gpu-node-32 'nvidia-smi --query-gpu=index,name,temperature.gpu,utilization.gpu,clocks.gr --format=csv,noheader'`

mike-sre: output: ```0, A100-SXM4-80GB, 92 C, 99 %, 11000 MHz```

mike-sre: ECC corrected errors rising: `cat /sys/class/drm/card0/ce_count` -> 124 correctable errs in last 10m. thermal_mgmt logs show fan at 98%.

alice-eng: that explains thermal throttle. streaming kernel is sensitive to small stalls (KV cache eviction + thermal slowdowns) and causes p99 spikes. mitigation options: 1) drain node from serving ring, 2) route traffic to dedicated warm standby, 3) enable fallback smaller model on affected routing prefixes.

kevin-support: customers seeing degraded completions for streaming (progress updates freeze then resume). CS ticket volume rising. we should set comms.

sarah (oncall): priority: live mitigation first. mike, can you remove gpu-node-32 from LB and start drain? steps?

mike-sre: `kubectl cordon node/gpu-node-32` then `./orchestrator evict --node gpu-node-32 --grace 30s --force` (we have streaming sessions; graceful drain 30s to allow KV checkpoint). Kicking now.

mike-sre: cordon done. starting eviction. watching active sessions: currently 412 streams. will trigger fallback routing for new sessions.

alice-eng: routing rule active: if node healthy=false, route to fallback pool 'dedicated-warm-2' and apply model fallback map to redwood-base-v2 -> redwood-base-v2-q4f (quantized) to reduce latency. toggling now.

alice-eng: toggled fallback. deploy-bot: route-change applied at 2026-03-15T08:47:12 UTC.

mike-sre: eviction hitting streaming tail. some sessions stuck due to KV handshake; issuing `evacuate --force-session-migrate` for critical sessions.

mike-sre: after eviction start, p99 dropped from 3.4s -> 1.8s in 2m. errors back down. still some tail spikes for in-flight streams.

kevin-support: posting to status page: "We are investigating increased streaming latency affecting a subset of requests in US-WEST-2. Mitigation in progress; some requests may experience delays." will update in 10m.

alice-eng: checking GPU telemetry: temperature slowly falling to 78 C, ECC correctables plateauing. suspect intermittent fan driver noise causing transient throttles.

mike-sre: hardware team pinged. @tom-hw can you look at telemetry and advise on post-incident steps (swap, burnin)?

 tom-hw: on it. initial analysis shows elevated correctable ECC counts + thermal cycles. recommend repro on bench with stress-test and PCIe retest, possible RMA if flakey. For now keep node in drain/quarantine.

sarah (oncall): agree. keep quarantined. open a hardware ticket and mark node out-of-rotation. mike, can you confirm traffic fully shifted and SLOs recovered?

mike-sre: traffic shifted. p95 steady ~430ms, p99 ~1.2s across region, error rate baseline. last 5m p99 = 1.15s. tagging incident as mitigated.

kevin-support: updating status: "Mitigation applied - traffic routed away from affected host. Customers may still see intermittent session stalls while sessions drain. No data loss reported. Engineers continue to monitor."

alice-eng: creating temp alert for ECC correctable rate on all nodes: `alert: GPU_ECC_CORRECTABLE_RATE > 10/min for 3m -> severity P2` to catch earlier in future.

mike-sre: snapshotting node logs and NVidia counters, uploading to incident page. `tar -czf /tmp/gpu-node-32-logs-6098765432.tgz /var/log/telemetry/* /var/log/kern.log` -> uploaded to INCIDENT page.

mike-sre: recording timeline in page + flagging for postmortem. next steps: hardware bench + replacement, review draining grace for streaming flows (30s might be too short for long-lived KV sessions), add routing guard to avoid single-node hot spots during high-traffic windows.

sarah (oncall): good. I'll hand off to monday oncall for post-incident follow-up; keeping incident channel open until hardware swap confirmed. thanks team. :heart:

incident-bot: INCIDENT MITIGATED - severity lowered to P2 at 2026-03-15T08:58:59 UTC. Remember to file postmortem within 72h and attach action items.
